## Start with your current skills

You do not need to complete every Python course. Choose the pathway that supports
the work you want to do, and use prerequisites to avoid being asked to guess at
skills a course assumes.

::: {.callout-tip title="New to programming?"}
Start with [Python Foundations](../courses/python-foundations/index.qmd). It is
the common entry point for both pathways and assumes no programming experience.
:::

## Software-development pathway

1. [Python Foundations](../courses/python-foundations/index.qmd)
2. [Intermediate Python: Applied Problem Solving](../courses/intermediate-python/index.qmd) — curriculum TBD
3. [Advanced Python: Complex Problem Solving](../courses/advanced-python/index.qmd) — curriculum TBD

Choose this route to apply Python to progressively less guided problems, then
solve complex problems with meaningful correctness, performance, and design
constraints. While those two applied courses are being designed, complete the
full [Python Foundations](../courses/python-foundations/index.qmd) sequence to
strengthen files, environments, testing, OOP, and reusable Python patterns.

## Scientific and data pathway

1. [Python Foundations](../courses/python-foundations/index.qmd)
2. [Scientific Computing with Python](../courses/scientific-python/index.qmd)
3. [Data Science and Machine Learning with Python](../courses/data-science-ml/index.qmd)

Choose this route to work with arrays, experiments, plots, tabular data, and
machine-learning models. Intermediate Python is recommended when your data or ML
work grows into a larger software project.

## Readiness guide

| If you can already... | Consider starting with... |
|---|---|
| Write small programs with conditions, loops, collections, and functions but have not used files, tests, or projects | Continue Python Foundations from Unit 3 |
| Independently parse, model, test, and explain unfamiliar small problems | Intermediate Python when its curriculum is published |
| Compare algorithms and handle state, scale, or performance constraints | Advanced Python when its curriculum is published |
| Use NumPy arrays, make plots, and explain a numerical experiment | Data Science and Machine Learning |
| Recognize some syntax but cannot yet explain or debug it confidently | Python Foundations |

When uncertain, open a prerequisite course and try its unit checkpoints. A
short review is usually faster than struggling with missing foundations.
